Cross-validate any learner with spatial folds

Source: R/cross-validation.R
cv_spatial.Rd

You supply fit_fn(train_sf), which fits on one fold's training rows and returns a spatial_fit; cv_spatial() builds or takes the folds, calls fit_fn once per fold, predicts the held-out rows and returns pooled and per-fold scores. cv_rf() is a wrapper over it.

Usage

cv_spatial(
  data_sf,
  response_var,
  predictor_vars,
  fit_fn,
  folds = NULL,
  k = 5,
  seed = 123,
  boundary = NULL,
  pointize = "auto",
  predict_args = list(),
  fold_info_fn = NULL,
  p = NULL,
  block_size = NULL,
  auto_range = FALSE,
  parallel = FALSE,
  metrics = NULL,
  .caller = "cv_spatial"
)

Arguments

data_sf

An sf layer with the response and the predictors.

response_var

Name of the response column.

predictor_vars

Character vector of predictor column names.

fit_fn

A function of one argument, the training slice of data_sf, returning a spatial_fit built with new_spatial_fit(). It is called once per fold on the training rows only, so anything done inside it (scaling, tuning, an inner variable sweep) is already nested and leak-free. The subclass it stamps must have a predict.<subclass>() method registered, since that is how each fold is scored. The fit models response_var (its response_var is the call's): a fold whose fit models another column fails, with the two names in fold_status, since its predictions are scored against response_var.

folds

Optional fold definitions, in one of three shapes: a make_folds() result; a bare list of list(train =, test =) pairs of ..row_id values; or a vector of fold labels, one per row, which becomes leave-that-label-out splits. The label vector is how folds built by another package are used here: blockCV::cv_spatial() returns one as $folds_ids, while its $folds_list holds two unnamed vectors per fold and is refused by name. Train and test must be disjoint; a fold that trains on its own test rows is not a cross-validation split and is refused with an error. IDs naming no row of the prepared data are dropped with a logged count (expected when rows were removed for missing values; a sign the folds came from other data when they were not). When NULL, the folds are make_folds(method = "block_kfold"), built with k, seed, boundary, block_size and auto_range. With folds = NULL the score estimates the error at the distance the block grid built here puts between the held-out points and their training data, which overstates the error of a map where the samples cover the area it predicts over. The excess is how much the model's error grows from the map's distances to the data to the block grid's, and is small for a model whose error changes little with the distance from the data. fold_separation() with prediction_points compares the held-out distances with those of the locations the model will predict at, and make_folds(method = "knndm", prediction_points = ) builds folds matched to them.

k

Number of folds to build when folds is NULL; not read when folds is supplied. Default 5.

seed

Seed for building the folds when folds is NULL, and for the one seed drawn per fold before fit_fn runs, so a learner that draws random numbers gives the same scores on every run, sequential or parallel. With a seed, the caller's random stream is restored afterwards. Default 123; NULL draws the per-fold seeds from the session's RNG state, and advances it.

boundary

Optional polygon layer (sf or sfc). Data without a CRS are aligned to it, and the blocks built when folds is NULL are clipped to it (see make_folds() and spatialkit-geometry).

pointize

How a feature that is not a point is reduced to one before fitting: a mode of coerce_to_points(). Default "auto".

predict_args

A list of extra arguments for predict() on each fold's fit.

fold_info_fn

Optional function(fit, test_sf, y, yhat) returning a named list (or a named vector) of per-fold extras (a bandwidth, a tuning value, anything read off the fitted object), added as columns of fold_metrics. It sees the fit and the held-out layer, which metrics does not; it is applied per fold only, and its values are not pooled. An element ..per_row that is a data frame with one row per held-out observation is spliced into predictions instead (NA in the rows of a fold that returned none; one of the wrong length is dropped and logged); its columns must be named, once, and not reuse a column predictions already has (..row_id, fold, y, yhat, y_train_mean). Every other element must be named, hold one value, and not reuse a column fold_metrics already has; anything else is an error. A fold_info_fn that throws on a fold is logged, its columns are NA for that fold, and fold_status$message says so; the fold is kept.

p

Number of predictors for the per-fold adjusted \(R^2\), or NULL to skip it. It applies only to models with one global parameter count; pass NULL for models with spatially varying coefficients, such as GWR.

block_size

Optional minimum block edge length, in the units of the CRS the folds are built in, for the blocks built when folds is NULL; see make_folds(). It is a size you choose and is compared with the autocorrelation range only when one can be estimated, in which case a smaller size is warned about. Beside supplied folds it has nothing to size and raises a warning of class spatialkit_fold_args_ignored.

auto_range

Logical, default FALSE. TRUE with folds = NULL estimates the autocorrelation range and uses it as the minimum block size. TRUE beside supplied folds raises the same warning as block_size.

parallel

Logical or positive integer. TRUE detects the number of cores and fits the folds in parallel with parallel::mclapply() (macOS and Linux; sequential on Windows); an integer above 1 uses that many cores. Default FALSE (sequential). A learner that runs OpenMP code (a function of GWmodel, or an xgboost built with GNU libgomp) can hang the forked workers once it has run in the session; keep such a fit_fn sequential.

metrics

Optional scoring function of your own; see the section "Your own metrics". Default NULL: the built-in metrics only.

.caller

For package wrappers; do not set it.

Value

A list with:

overall

One row of metrics pooled over the held-out rows of every fold that produced predictions.

fold_metrics

One row per fold that produced predictions: fold, n_train, n_test, n_pred, the metrics, and the columns of fold_info_fn and metrics.

predictions

One row per held-out row scored: ..row_id, fold, y, yhat and y_train_mean, the mean response of that fold's training rows.

folds

The splits as run, each with its fold_id.

n_folds_attempted, n_folds_succeeded

The folds supplied (or built) and the folds scored. A fit_fn that fails on every fold otherwise looks like a run that scored NA, so compare the two before reading overall.

fold_status

A data frame with one row per fold supplied: fold, status and message. status is one of

  • "ok": message is empty unless fold_info_fn failed on the fold;

  • "error": the fit or its predict() threw, and message is the error text;

  • "skipped": nothing to score (too few matched rows, a prediction of the wrong length, or no finite pair of observed and predicted values);

  • "dropped": an empty test set, or fewer than two training rows once incomplete rows were removed, so the fold never reached the fitter;

  • "worker_error": a parallel worker died, for example killed for lack of memory.

Every fold missing from fold_metrics has its reason here, after the console output of a long run is gone.

orphan_rows

The ..row_ids of rows in the data that no fold names: they enter no training set and are never scored. It is empty unless the folds were built on a different or subsetted layer.

n_unknown_ids

The number of distinct row IDs the folds name that the data do not have (expected when rows were removed for missing values). Each such row is named by every fold, once as a test row and once in each other fold's training set, and this counts the row, not the mentions.

n_dropped

The number of rows prep_model_data() removed for missing or non-finite values or a bad geometry before any fold was fitted.

A failure costs that fold only: with parallel = TRUE each fold runs in its own worker, and a sequential run catches the error per fold. An error that stops a sequential run (a metrics or fold_info_fn return value of the wrong shape) stops a parallel one too, naming the fold. When some folds, but not all, end as "error", "skipped" or "worker_error", the function warns, naming them and how many rows overall covers: it is pooled over the folds that produced predictions, and the fold that fails is often the hardest to predict, so it may flatter the model. A "dropped" fold has its own warning.

The fold column of fold_metrics, predictions and fold_status carries the fold's index in the folds object that was supplied, so it lines up with make_folds()$assignment$fold even when some folds were unusable and dropped. Splits that already carry a fold_id, as the folds of a cv_*() result do, keep it: handing one run's folds to another labels each fold as the first run and fold_separation() do, a dropped fold's gap included.

R2 is the out-of-sample \(R^2\): the total sum of squares is taken about the mean of the training rows (in overall, each held-out row about its own fold's training mean), the null prediction available when the fold is predicted, and not about the held-out rows' own mean, a null model that would know the test data. On spatial blocks the two can differ widely; R2 is below 0 when the model predicts worse than the training mean. model_metrics(newdata = ) uses the same baseline. overall$Adj_R2 is always NA: the pooled out-of-sample predictions come from k separately fitted models and have no single parameter count to adjust for. The per-fold fold_metrics$Adj_R2 carries the adjusted value when p is supplied, and is NA otherwise. A fit_fn that returns a gwr_fit of a response at a large offset gives predictions the columns y_centre, yhat_centred and y_train_mean_centred (see cv_gwr()).

Name collision with blockCV

The blockCV package exports a function of the same name that does the opposite job: blockCV::cv_spatial() builds spatial folds, where this function runs a cross-validation over folds it is given. With both packages attached, whichever was attached last masks the other; spatialkit::cv_spatial() always resolves to this one. The two work together: blockCV::cv_spatial() returns its fold assignment as $folds_ids, a vector of fold labels, and that vector is accepted as the folds argument here and in every other cv_*() function.

Your own metrics

The built-in columns (RMSE, MAE, MAPE, SMAPE, R2, Adj_R2) are the Gaussian regression set; see "Which metrics survive a non-Gaussian response" in model_metrics() for which of them hold up on a count or a bounded response. metrics scores what they cannot: a function(y, yhat) that returns a named numeric vector (a named list of scalars, or a one-row data frame, also serve), for example a Poisson deviance, a log score on a probability, or a loss with your own weights. It is applied twice, as the built-in metrics are: once per fold, to that fold's held-out rows, so each name becomes a column of fold_metrics; and once to the pooled out-of-sample predictions of every fold, so each name becomes a column of overall. Only the pairs the built-in metrics use reach the function (both y and yhat finite), so its columns describe the same rows as RMSE, and n_pred counts them.

The contract: every element named, names unique and not one of the built-in column names, one number per name. The built-in names include the per-fold extras of the backend or of your fold_info_fn (bandwidth for cv_gwr(); CRPS, coverage_*, gp_k, gp_n_basis and n_draws for cv_bayes()), and mean_CRPS, which compare_models_cv() writes. Anything else is an error, since a scoring function that returns the wrong shape is a mistake to report, not a fold to skip. A function that throws on a fold is logged and its columns are NA for that fold (and for overall, if it throws on the pooled predictions); a fold is never dropped for it. When no fold produced a prediction the empty fold_metrics frame still carries the function's columns, typed, provided the function can be called on zero-length input.

fold_info_fn is the per-fold half of the same mechanism, with access to the fitted object and the held-out layer; metrics sees only the two vectors but is also pooled. compare_models_cv() hands one metrics to every backend, so the columns are comparable across the rows of its overall.

Warnings a learner raises in every fold

A warning from a fold's fit or from its predict() reaches the caller as it is raised, so a learner that warns in every fold warns once per fold. Two groups of the package's own warnings are collected over the folds instead and raised once per call, under this function's name and with the class they had:

  • the two in which predict() on a GWR counts locations ("spatialkit_gwr_not_estimable" and "spatialkit_gwr_extrapolation"), with the totals over the folds that had any, as cv_gwr() raises them (see predict.gwr_fit());

  • the four fit_bayesian_spatial_model() raises about a fit, naming the folds, as cv_bayes() raises them (see the section "Warnings from the folds" there).

With parallel above one core a fold's warnings are raised after the folds have run, once per distinct text; one of the package's own classes keeps its class and its fields.

Percentage errors on responses with zeros

MAPE divides by the observed value and SMAPE by \(|y| + |\hat{y}|\), so neither is defined where its denominator is zero. Neither returns Inf or NaN. Both are averaged over the rows whose denominator is non-zero, and are NA when no row qualifies. Non-zero is judged at the scale of the data: a denominator no larger than 100 machine epsilons times the largest one counts as zero, so the rule does not depend on the units of the response. The n_MAPE and n_SMAPE columns record how many rows that was; the n column (n_pred in a cross-validation result) counts finite observation/prediction pairs. Read a percentage error next to that count: when n_MAPE is smaller, MAPE is an average over a subset of the data, whatever its value.

Any response taking exact zeros is affected: counts, rainfall, abundance, claim amounts. On a zero-inflated response with 62 zeros out of 120, MAPE averages the 58 non-zero rows and n_MAPE is 58. SMAPE drops the rows where observation and prediction are both near zero, which on a well-fitted zero-inflated model are the rows it got right, so it averages the harder rows only and reads worse than the fit deserves. n_SMAPE shows how many rows it kept; it does not correct the average.

RMSE, MAE and \(R^2\) use every finite row; prefer them whenever the response can be zero. For a Bayesian GP fit, cv_bayes() also reports CRPS and interval coverage, which are proper scoring rules and are defined at zero.

See also

new_spatial_fit() for the constructor a fit_fn must use; cv_gwr(), cv_bayes() and cv_rf() for the built-in backends.

Other cross-validation: compare_models_cv(), cv_bayes(), cv_gwr(), cv_rf(), plot_calibration(), plot_cv_metrics()

Examples

library(sf)
set.seed(1)
n <- 80
site <- st_as_sf(
  data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000),
             elev = rnorm(n)),
  coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632
)
site$price <- 10 + 0.01 * (st_coordinates(site)[, 1] - 5e5) +
  2 * site$elev + rnorm(n)

# 1. A fit_fn returning a spatial_fit of your own subclass.
lm_fit <- function(train_sf) {
  new_spatial_fit(
    subclass       = "lm_fit",
    engine         = lm(price ~ elev, st_drop_geometry(train_sf)),
    formula        = price ~ elev,
    response_var   = "price",
    predictor_vars = "elev",
    data_sf        = train_sf
  )
}

# 2. The predict() method cv_spatial() scores each fold with. Without it
#    every fold fails and `overall` comes back all-NA.
predict.lm_fit <- function(object, newdata = NULL, ...) {
  if (is.null(newdata)) newdata <- object$data_sf
  as.numeric(stats::predict(object$engine, st_drop_geometry(newdata)))
}
registerS3method("predict", "lm_fit", predict.lm_fit)

cv <- cv_spatial(site, "price", "elev", fit_fn = lm_fit, k = 3, seed = 1)
#> cv_spatial(): no folds supplied -- using spatial block k-fold CV (k=3).
cv$overall
#>       RMSE      MAE     MAPE    SMAPE        R2 Adj_R2 n_pred n_MAPE n_SMAPE
#> 1 3.472328 3.009688 21.29953 20.27029 0.2341257     NA     80     80      80
# Compare these before reading the metrics above; fold_status says why
# any fold is missing from fold_metrics.
c(attempted = cv$n_folds_attempted, succeeded = cv$n_folds_succeeded)
#> attempted succeeded 
#>         3         3 
cv$fold_status
#>   fold status message
#> 1    1     ok        
#> 2    2     ok        
#> 3    3     ok        

# 3. A metric of your own beside the built-in ones: per fold and pooled.
med_ae <- function(y, yhat) c(MedAE = stats::median(abs(y - yhat)))
cv2 <- cv_spatial(site, "price", "elev", fit_fn = lm_fit, k = 3, seed = 1,
                  metrics = med_ae)
#> cv_spatial(): no folds supplied -- using spatial block k-fold CV (k=3).
cv2$overall$MedAE
#> [1] 2.981173
cv2$fold_metrics[, c("fold", "RMSE", "MedAE")]
#>   fold     RMSE    MedAE
#> 1    1 3.793601 3.536960
#> 2    2 3.198481 2.590833
#> 3    3 3.359840 2.678648
